title: URL Filtering rule fields where the Python SDK, Terraform provider and help disagree

prose.text: Three layers describe URL Filtering rule fields, and they disagree in places. The action semantics are in [[zia.url-filtering.actions]], the tenant-wide advanced settings in [[zia.url-filtering.advanced-settings]], and the Go SDK's defects in [[zia.sdk-go.service-defects]].

prose.label: Isolate.
prose.text: {{tf-isolate-get-workaround}} The provider's own checks on an ISOLATE rule are in [[zia.terraform.url-filtering-rules:isolate-validation]].

prose.label: Size quota.
prose.text: {{size-quota-help-mb}} {{size-quota-code-kb}} The schema label disagrees with the provider's behavior and docs {{divergence:size-quota-unit}}.

prose.label: Description round trip.
prose.text: {{tf-description-diff-suppression}} Whether the server itself rewrites whitespace is open {{gap:description-server-normalized}}.

checks.do: Which unit a size quota is in before trusting a migrated value: help says MB, the Terraform schema text and the Python docstring say KB.
Whether an ISOLATE rule meets the provider's checks, which are listed in the Terraform subject.
Whether a plan-time description diff is whitespace only, since the provider suppresses equal-after-normalizing text.

per-rule-cipa-flag.statement: A URL Filtering rule has its own ciparule boolean, and the advanced URL filter and cloud app settings carry a separate enable_cipa_compliance setting.

quotes: ciparule (bool): The CIPA compliance rule is enabled if this is set to `True`. Defaults to `False`.
Updates the URL and Cloud App Control advanced policy settings
enable_cipa_compliance (bool): Enables the predefined CIPA Compliance Rule.

tf-action-values.statement: The Terraform provider accepts BLOCK, CAUTION, ALLOW and ISOLATE as a URL Filtering rule action.

evidence.after: Description: "Action taken when traffic matches rule criteria",

python-action-values.statement: The Python SDK documents the rule action as ANY, NONE, BLOCK, CAUTION, ALLOW or ICAP_RESPONSE, without ISOLATE.

tf-isolate-get-workaround.statement: The provider works around an API bug in which a GET of an ISOLATE rule returns cbiProfileId but not the cbiProfile object, by keeping the profile from state.

quotes: Workaround for API bug: GET does not return the cbiProfile object for ISOLATE rules,
Preserve the cbi_profile from state when the API doesn't return it.

size-quota-help-mb.statement: The console help gives the URL Filtering size quota minimum as 10 MB and maximum as 100,000 MB.

quotes: The minimum value you can enter is 10 MB and the maximum value is 100,000 MB.
evidence.after: Select this to allow access to all sites in the selected URL categories.

size-quota-code-kb.statement: The Terraform schema description says KB, but the provider validates 10-100000 as MB (as its docs say) and converts to KB (x1024) before sending; the API wire unit is KB, per the Python docstring.

quotes: Size quota in MB beyond which the URL Filtering rule is applied.
Size quota in KB beyond which the URL Filtering rule is applied.
size_quota (str): Size quota in KB for applying the URL Filtering rule.
return 0, fmt.Errorf("size_quota must be between %d MB and %d MB", minMB, maxMB)

tf-description-diff-suppression.statement: The provider suppresses a diff on a URL Filtering rule's description when the old and new text are equal after trimming each line and normalizing the trailing newline.

quotes: // Ensure uniform indentation by trimming each line
// Ensure the final newline to match Terraform formatting

description-server-normalized.title: Whether the ZIA API rewrites a rule description's whitespace and line endings
description-server-normalized.detail: Unverified legacy statement: The earlier reference said what is PUT as a URL Filter rule description is not what GET returns because the server normalizes whitespace and line endings; the provider's diff suppression is consistent with that but no vendored source shows the server doing it.
description-server-normalized.blocks: Whether a description round trip shows false drift from the server, or only from the provider.

size-quota-unit.summary: The Terraform schema description labels size_quota as KB, but the provider validates and accepts it as MB, as its documentation and the console help say, and converts to KB for the wire.

positions.says: size_quota is in KB, validated between 10 and 100,000 (schema description).

quotes: Size quota in KB beyond which the URL Filtering rule is applied.

positions.says: The provider validates the value as MB (10 to 100,000) and multiplies by 1024 to send KB.

quotes: size_quota must be between %d MB and %d MB

positions.says: The provider documentation says the size quota is in MB.

quotes: Size quota in MB beyond which the URL Filtering rule is applied.

size-quota-unit.impact: HCL values are megabytes; the schema label is stale. Reading the label as KB, or treating the Python SDK's KB value as an HCL value, is off by a factor of 1024.

action-values-differ.summary: The Python SDK's documented action values omit ISOLATE, which the Terraform provider accepts, while the SDK adds ANY, NONE and ICAP_RESPONSE.

positions.says: Actions are ANY, NONE, BLOCK, CAUTION, ALLOW and ICAP_RESPONSE.
Actions are BLOCK, CAUTION, ALLOW and ISOLATE.

evidence.after: Description: "Action taken when traffic matches rule criteria",

action-values-differ.impact: A tool that validates actions against the Python docstring would reject an ISOLATE rule that exists in the tenant, and one that validates against the provider would reject ICAP_RESPONSE.
